ai_summary: Great Britain’s wind fleet is currently delivering 15.8 GW across the transmission system, with estimated Scottish wind output contributing 5.3 GW, representing 52.5% of installed Scottish wind capacity. Driven by this strong regional renewable output, Scottish carbon intensity has plunged to a clean 2 gCO2/kWh, standing in sharp contrast to 70 gCO2/kWh GB-wide. However, cross-border transmission bottlenecks continue to limit power transfers to southern demand centers. As a result, Scottish generation curtailed so far today has reached 10.6 GWh through Balancing Mechanism actions, incurring a constraint cost of about £587,621. To compensate for this constrained clean electricity, thermal plant dispatched elsewhere has consumed an estimated 2,017,344 cubic meters of gas, releasing an unnecessary 3,716 tonnes of CO2 into the atmosphere. Annualizing today's constraint expenditure implies a total yearly cost of approximately £214 million. Recovered via nationwide balancing charges, this constraint burden adds an estimated £0.80/MWh to everybody's invoice in the UK. Accelerated transmission reinforcement across the Anglo-Scottish boundary remains urgently needed to curb these counterproductive emissions, unlock trapped zero-carbon power, and reduce system costs for consumers.
